newsitem.title: USA: Heavy freeze damage hits 24 pct of Oklahoma wheat.
newsitem.headline: Heavy freeze damage hits 24 pct of Oklahoma wheat.

text.p: Nearly one-fourth of Oklahoma's wheat crop sustained heavy damage as a result of the April 11-13 freeze, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop weather report.
Damage to the state's wheat crop was assessed as 24 percent heavy, 38 moderate, 29 light and nine undamaged.

Overall, the state's wheat condition was rated at 12 percent very poor, 23 poor, 36 fair, 28 good and one percent excellent. That marked a further decline from last Monday's rating of 16 percent very poor, eight poor, 34 fair, 38 good and four percent excellent.

"Damage...varied from field to field, depending upon the planting date, variety, moisture condition and degree of grazing," the report said. "The Panhandle, Southwest and South Central districts were dealt the heaviest blows."
Meanwhile, 33 percent of the wheat acreage was heading, compared to 24 last year and 40 for the five-year average.
Late-week rains and cool temperatures slowed wheat growth and aided the filling of heads. The mild weather allowed plants to recover from the freeze but hindered plantings.
Two percent of the state's intended sorghum acreage was planted, versus three last year and five on average.
